headline: Growth accelerates, outlook raised past a calendar drag
summary_short: Aramark's fiscal Q3 2026 revenue rose 9.3% y/y to $5,058M and operating income grew 18.1% y/y to $216M; GAAP diluted EPS climbed 33.3% y/y to $0.36 even after a 53rd-week calendar shift the company says cut revenue growth by ~2 points and operating-income growth by an estimated 11 points.
summary_long: Revenue growth was broad-based: FSS United States +7.7% (Sports/Leisure/Corrections, Business & Industry, Healthcare) and FSS International +13.2% (Spain, Canada, U.K., Germany). Operating income grew 18.1% y/y on higher revenue, supply-chain efficiencies, and cost management, more than offsetting the calendar-shift drag; lower interest expense ($79.9M vs $86.4M y/y) lifted net income 36.1% to $98M. Cash was roughly flat y/y at $499M despite stronger free cash flow, after $67M of YTD buybacks and $95M of YTD dividends. Aramark raised its FY2026 Organic Revenue growth outlook to +9-10% (from 'high end of +7-9%') and reaffirmed AOI growth (+12-17%), Adjusted EPS growth (+20-25%), and a leverage ratio under 3.0x.

drivers.explanation: CEO Zillmer cited industry-leading client retention (~98%), record new client wins (+51% y/y, $1.6B+ YTD), and continued Aramark Nexus expansion into AI data-center hospitality as behind another quarter of strong top- and bottom-line growth.

Broad-based net new business and base business momentum: FSS US led by Sports/Leisure/Corrections, Business & Industry, and Healthcare; FSS International broad-based across Spain, Canada, U.K., Germany. The FY2025 53rd-week calendar shift cut growth by an estimated 2 points.

Strong revenue, supply-chain efficiencies, and productivity gains from cost management drove growth; the calendar shift reduced operating-income growth by an estimated 11 points (would have been ~29% without it).
Net income grew faster than operating income because interest expense fell to $79.9M from $86.4M y/y, adding a second tailwind on top of the operating-line gain.
Diluted EPS grew roughly in line with net income (+36.1%) since diluted share count rose only 1.2% y/y, so per-share dilution was a minor offset.
